flashcard_questions.q: What are the products when an acid reacts with a metal?
What are the products when an acid reacts with a base?
What are the products when an acid reacts with a metal carbonate?
flashcard_questions.a: A salt plus water and carbon dioxide gas.

flashcard_questions.q: How do you test a gas to show it is hydrogen?
flashcard_questions.a: A burning splint makes it burn with a squeaky pop.

flashcard_questions.q: Which metals do not react with dilute acids?
flashcard_questions.a: Those below hydrogen in the reactivity series, such as copper and gold.

flashcard_questions.q: Which two ions react together in every neutralisation reaction?
What is an alkali in chemistry?
flashcard_questions.a: A base that dissolves in water.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of salt does hydrochloric acid always produce?
Which type of salt does sulfuric acid always produce?
Which type of salt does nitric acid always produce?
In the soluble salt practical, why is the base added in excess?
flashcard_questions.a: To make sure all the acid has reacted, so the crystals stay pure.

flashcard_questions.q: What range does the pH scale run over?

flashcard_questions.a: One that completely ionises in water, releasing all its hydrogen ions.
One that only partially ionises in water, reaching an equilibrium.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) Why does a strong acid have a lower pH than a weak acid of the same concentration?
flashcard_questions.a: It releases more hydrogen ions into the solution.
